name: Axial resistor, 1/4 W (through-hole)
blurb: Quarter-watt resistor with a lead on each end, bent to fit holes 10.16 mm (0.4 inch) apart; the value is set per project.

pins.note: Resistors have no polarity: either lead goes either way.

verify: The drawn body is the envelope of the lead span (10.16 mm) with a 2.3 mm diameter body assumed; a typical 1/4 W body is about 6.3 mm long and 2.3 mm across, but varies by maker (carbon film is slightly larger). Not read from a drawing. Lead pitch is the fitting pitch, not the part: leads can be bent to 7.62 mm or 5.08 mm. Measure your resistors if the enclosure sits close. Drawing-only fields on the pins: z -1.15 puts each lead on the axis of the 2.3 mm body; lead 20 mm is a typical length left on a taped resistor, not read from a drawing.
sources: Typical 1/4 W axial (DIN 0207) body size and 0.4 inch fitting pitch; no manufacturer drawing opened
